title: Isolation of myeloid cells from mouse brain tumors for single-cell RNA-seq analysis
protocol: Homogenize brain tumor at room temperature.
Resect brain tumor.
Cut skull along the sagittal suture.
Remove skull.
Remove the brain starting at the frontal lobe.
Disconnect nerve fibers from the brainstem.
Euthanize the mouse.
Remove the head of the mouse using a pair of scissors.
Cut away the skin until the brain stem can be seen.
Starting from the brain stem, cut upward along the sagittal suture applying as little pressure as possible to the brain itself.
Peel each hemisphere of the skull away from the brain to the side.
With a spatula or forceps, remove the brain from the base of the skull and cut long nerve fibers to detach the brain.
Gently push the cerebellum with tumor away from the brainstem.
Detach the nerve fibers connecting the cerebellum to the brainstem.
Perfuse mouse with 10 mL ice-cold PBS through the left ventricle prior to resection for highly vascularized tumors.
Add 5 mL RPMI solution and tumor into a 10 mL glass homogenizer and homogenize tissue.
Place a 70 μm cell filter on a 50 mL conical tube and pipette onto it the homogenate to filter out cell clumps.
Transfer the flow through into a 15 mL conical tube.
To cell suspension, add RPMI solution to make a total of 7 mL.
Add 3 mL SIP to cell suspension and mix by pipetting to create 10 mL cell suspension in 30% Percoll.
Take up 5 mL of 70% Percoll solution in a 5 mL syringe attached to a spinal needle.
Insert the needle into the cell suspension until the bevel reaches the bottom of the conical tube.
Gently and slowly eject 70% Percoll layer below the 30% Percoll cell suspension layer.
Pipette 5 mL of 70% Percoll solution into a 15 mL tube.
Slowly pipette 10 mL of cell suspension in 30% Percoll onto the 70% Percoll solution.
Centrifuge the gradient mixture at 500 × g for 30 min with maximal acceleration and zero deceleration to eliminate turbulence.
Set the centrifuge acceleration to maximal speed and deceleration to 0.
Prepare a stock Isotonic Percoll SIP 100% (SIP100) solution.
Determine the volume of SIP100 needed per sample from the provided table.
Bring cell suspension volume up to 6 mL.
Add 4 mL of SIP100 to make 10 mL of a 40% Percoll cell suspension.
Layer 80% Percoll beneath the 40% Percoll layer as described above.
Spin at 325 × g for 30 minutes.
Gently remove the tube from the centrifuge after spinning.
Aspirate and discard the top white layer containing myelin fragments.
Using a spinal needle attached to a 5 mL syringe, insert the needle into the gradient until the tip hits the interface layer.
Gently aspirate into the syringe the interface layer (∼2–3 mL).
Transfer the aspirated mixture gently to a fresh 15 mL conical tube.
Add ice-cold 12 mL MACS buffer to wash cells and remove Percoll.
Mix with gentle pipetting.
Reset centrifuge deceleration back to maximum and temperature to 4°C.
Spin cell suspension at 300 × g for 7 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of cold MACs buffer and transfer to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Spin the cell suspension at 300 × g speed for 1 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 90 μL of MACs buffer (per 10^7 total cells).
Incubate cell suspension with CD11b MicroBeads by adding 10 μL of microbeads to every 90 μL of cell suspension and incubate for 15 min on ice.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of MACS buffer and spin at 300 × g for 10 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 500 μL of cold MACS buffer with gentle pipetting.
Set up an LS column in the MidiMACS separator mounted to a MACS Multistand over a 15 mL conical tube.
Apply the cell suspension onto the column and wait for the solution to run through the column.
Wash the column 3 times with 3 mL cold MACS buffer.
Pipette 5 mL of cold MACS buffer onto the column and immediately flush out magnetically labeled cells by applying and pushing the plunger.
Spin at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatant.
Add 1 mL cold MACS buffer to cell pellet.
Mix gently with pipetting.
Transfer cell suspension to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Spin at 500 × g for 1 minute.
Remove as much supernatant as possible.
Resuspend cells in desired volume and buffer appropriate for the scRNA-sequencing platform.
For 10× Genomics, use 1× PBS (calcium and magnesium free) containing 0.04% weight/volume BSA (400 μg/mL).
If the desired volume is uncertain, resuspend cells in about 50–100 μL of buffer.
Adjust volume after cell counting as needed.
Buffer should not contain excessive amounts of EDTA (>0.1 mM) or magnesium (>3 mM).
Pipette gently and slowly during cell resuspension steps.
Use wide-bore pipette tips to minimize cell damage.
Count the number of viable cells using trypan blue and a hemocytometer.
Check cell suspensions visually for debris or cell aggregates.
Filter cell suspension with Flowmi™ Cell Strainer (40 micron) if necessary.
Filter cell suspension with MACS SmartStrainer (30 micron) if necessary.
Re-pellet the supernatant at a higher centrifugation speed if cell concentration is lower than expected.
Dilute or concentrate the solution to obtain a cell suspension concentration between 700 and 1200 cells/μL for optimal chip loading.
Place the cells on ice immediately once the target cell concentration is obtained.
Load the cell suspension onto the chip for library preparation as soon as possible, ideally within 30 min.
Prepare a Chromium Next GEM Chip G in a Chromium Next GEM Secondary Holder.
Dispense 50% glycerol into all unused wells of the prepared chip.
Prepare the barcode master mix using RT Reagent B, Template Switch Oligo, Reducing Agent B, and RT Enzyme C.
Add cell suspension to the master mix (with/without water depending on the stock concentration).
Mix by pipetting.
Load 70 μL of final mixture into row 1 of the chip.
Load 50 μL of vortexed gel beads into row 2.
Wait 30 seconds after adding the gel beads.
Place a gasket over the chip and attach it to the Secondary Holder.
Attach the chip to the Chromium Single Cell Controller instrument for GEM generation.
Perform GEM-RT step in a thermal cycler: incubate at 53°C for 45 minutes, then at 85°C for 5 minutes, and hold at 4°C.
Add Recovery Agent after GEM-RT step.
Invert to mix and allow biphasic mixture to separate.
Add a master mix containing Dynabead MyOne SILANE beads, Reducing Agent B, Cleanup Buffer and water.
Incubate for 10 min with pipet mixing at 5 min.
Place tubes on 10× Magnetic Separator (High position) until the solution clears.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash beads with ethanol.
Elute with elution buffer.
Place on magnet to pull down beads.
Transfer 35 μL of sample to a new tube.
Add Amp Mix and cDNA Primers to the sample.
Place the sample in the thermal cycler according to the protocol.
Clean the cDNA by adding SPRIselect Reagent to make a final 0.6× solution.
Incubate for 5 min.
Place on magnet until solution clears.
Remove supernatant.
Wash beads with ethanol twice.
Place on magnet and remove residual ethanol.
Elute cDNA with elution buffer.
Perform quality control with a 1:10 diluted sample using the D1000 High Sensitivity kit.
Start the construction of dual index library by using 10 μL of cDNA sample.
Perform fragmentation, end-repair, and A-tailing in a joint reaction.
Purify the sample using a dual-sided 0.6×/0.8× bead:sample ratio with SPRIselect Reagent.
Mix each sample with a master mix consisting of ligation buffer, DNA ligase, and Adapter Oligo for adapter ligation.
Perform post-ligation cleanup with 0.8× SPRIselect Reagent purification.
Perform sample indexing PCR using Amp Mix and Dual Index TT Set A.
Follow the indexing PCR with a final size-selection process using a dual-sided 0.6×/0.8× bead:sample ratio.
Dilute the final library to a 1:10 ratio for analysis.
Run the diluted library on a Bioanalyzer or TapeStation High Sensitivity kits.
Verify that the typical size distribution of final libraries is between 300 and 1000 bp.
Analyze the trace quality, aiming for high-grade sample characteristics similar to those shown in standard reference figures.
Determine the average fragment size from the trace for accurate library quantification.
Sequence the library on the NovaSeq 6000 using the run parameters recommended by the 10× user guide.
Generate three files: barcodes.tsv, genes.tsv, and matrix.mtx using Cell Ranger with instructions from the tutorial.
Analyze the sequencing data using Seurat in R or R Studio.
Consider integrating data to eliminate batch effects when combining samples run at different times.
Annotate immune cells using key markers for specific cell types.
Use SingleR algorithm to import data from the Immgen database as a library reference.
Import published data from Li et al., 2019 as a library reference.
Alternatively, sequence samples of homeostatic microglia from a normal brain.
Batch sequenced peripheral blood from a mouse without tumor together with tumor-associated macrophages.
